title: The Royal Society: a journal outlives its founder
findings: Introduced Oldenburg and the journal; removed an instruction to collect comparison cases from public gaps and explained the uncertainty about prestige.

title: Lysenkoism: when authority can overrule evidence
findings: Removed the unrelated famine verification note and archival-reading diary; retained the distinction between changing doctrine and rebuilding institutions.

title: The Manhattan Project: coordination at enormous human cost
findings: Removed GFT narration and scope disclaimers; connected authority, resources, and displacement directly without treating mission achievement as public benefit.

title: Apollo: a clear goal still needed a coalition
findings: Replaced descriptions of historians’ arguments with the coalition and contracting arrangements; removed unintroduced later-decline dispute.

title: Challenger: warnings that did not reach the decision
findings: Removed GFT decline narration, generic anti-bureaucracy rebuttal, and research to-dos; kept concrete limits on causal interpretation.

title: COTS: public capability helps build private capability
findings: Removed source-access diary and government-versus-founder rebuttal; described demonstrations, termination, and financing directly.

title: Roman adoption: an heir is also a political alliance
findings: Removed GFT/Gibbon comparisons and an unintroduced detour into Trajan; made the restricted successor pool and political support the subject.

title: The Tetrarchy: a succession design that needed its designer
findings: Removed a GFT hypothesis presented as an observation and replaced the monograph-reading note with the unresolved succession mechanism.

title: Botswana: continuity also survives an opposition victory
findings: Introduced the opposition handover directly; removed an argument with GFT’s monarchy analogy and vague references to a development study.

title: Japanese adopted heirs: succession beyond the bloodline
findings: Kept research attribution where results depend on studies, but removed caricatured universal claims and internal requests to read tables.

title: Confucian transmission: preserving a tradition by changing it
findings: Removed the book-summary frame and unintroduced disputed authorship claims; explained transmission, reinterpretation, and uncertainty about origins directly.

title: Latter-day Saint missions: recruitment is not retention
findings: Removed reviewed-source narration and source-access diary; introduced centralized administration and kept retention distinct from recruitment.

title: Protestant literacy: competing explanations for prosperity
findings: Removed GFT narration and research-workflow instructions; retained the specific disagreement between literacy/prosperity and city-growth findings.

title: FOGBANK: documentation is not a living capability
findings: Removed GFT narration, comparison to an unintroduced ten-year claim, and a duplicate report presented as a separate observation; kept the nontechnical capability-loss account.

title: Bell Labs: discovery and diffusion need different arrangements
findings: Replaced source-description and replication-package notes with the distinction between patent access, market entry, and continuing research investment.

title: Xerox PARC: invention needs a route into the world
findings: Removed a rebuttal to the unintroduced myth that Xerox commercialized nothing and the source-shopping instructions; kept retrospective uncertainty relevant to the business decisions.

title: NUMMI: changing the work changed the culture
findings: Kept participant attribution for performance reports, but removed abstract-access commentary and the generic demand for more sources.

title: Surgical checklists: a form is not an implementation
findings: Retained the differing study outcomes and design limits; removed clinical-scope boilerplate and instructions to conduct another literature review.
